sentences.text:
By way of this petition filed under Section 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, the petitioner has prayed for quashing of FIR No.47 of 2019, dated 02.09.2019, registered under Sections 363, 366,
376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of POCSO Act, at Women Police Station Solan, District Solan, H.P.
2.
The petitioner as well as respondent No. 2, present in person in the Court.

The statement of respondent No.2, are who has since attained the majority, as well as the mother of respondent No.2,
who has been duly identified by the learned counsel appearing for respondent No.2, stand separately recorded, in which, both .
(respondent No.2 and her mother) have stated that in view of the subsequent developments and in view of the issue, which resulted in the lodging of the FIR having been amicably settled between the parties, they have no objections, in case, this petition is allowed by quashing the FIR as well as the ensuing criminal proceedings.

Respondent No.2 and her mother have also deposed in the Court that the amount of Rs. 1,00,000/-
which was received from the State Exchequer on account of the FIR, having been lodged under the provisions of POCSO Act, shall be refunded back to the State Government through the office of Child Development Project Officer Solan, H.P., by way of preparation of a bank draft for an amount of Rs.
1,00,000/- within 15 days from today.
3. Taking into consideration the fact that the parties have amicably resolved the issues between themselves and the victim/respondent No.2 is no more willing to continue with the criminal proceedings and also the fact that she happens to be a young girl and continuation of the proceedings would obviously affect her future life prospects also, the present petition is allowed and FIR No. 47 of 2019, dated 20.09.2019, registered under Sections 363, 366, 376 of the Indian Penal Code and Section 4 of POCSO Act, at Women Police Station Solan, District Solan, H.P., is quashed and set aside.

The statements of the complainant/respondent No. 2 as well as her mother .
made today in the Court shall form part of the judgment.
Miscellaneous applications, if any, also stand disposed of.

4. It is directed that the amount of Rs. 1,00,000/- which has been received by respondent No.2/her parents, as the case may be, shall stand refunded back to the State by way of bank draft drawn in 5. to the name of CDPO Solan, H.P., within a fortnight from today.

Though the matter stands disposed of on merit, but for the compliance of the order, in terms whereof, respondent No.2 has been directed to deposit the amount with the CDPO Solan, H.P., to come up on 19.06.2023.

sentences.text: Before the proceedings in this petition are closed, it is relevant to mention that a perusal of the documents appended with the petition demonstrate that name of the victim, who was a minor at the time when the FIR was lodged has been mentioned in the FIR itself, which is appended with the petition as Annexure P-1.

On umpteen numbers of occasions, this Court has called upon the State functionaries to sensitize the machinery of Police Department to ensure that the name of minor victim is not reflected in the documents, but it appears that no serious heed is being paid in this regard by the Department.
Taking into consideration the seriousness of the issue, the Court requested learned Advocate General to be present in the Court, who is present in the Court.

It is directed that learned Advocate .
General shall ensure that either from the Home Department or from the office of Director General of Police, instructions in black and white be issued to all the Authorities/Officers/Officials concerned that henceforth there should not be any complacency in the observation of the direction that the name of the minor victim should not be reflected in the FIRs/Rapat/Rojnamcha or any other document prepared in the course of investigation and let the instructions also spell out as to what action an erring Officers/Officials would be liable to face in case he or she commits the omission of mentioning the name of minor victim in any document.
Let personal compliance affidavits of both Principal Secretary (Home) as well as Director General of Police to the Government of Himachal Pradesh be filed on or before 19.06.2023.
( Ajay Mohan Goel) Judge May 22, 2023 (Vinod)
